articles.title: Connect your Westy window with 8 West ID
articles.summary: Start in Westy, check the account and computer in your browser, then return to the window to finish connecting.

blocks.text: **Purpose and prerequisites.** Open Westy from its icon in the system tray on Windows or the menu bar on a Mac. Its window shows your portal pages. If you already see your private chat, you can use it. To connect a signed-out window, use your own 8 West ID for the business.

items: In the Westy window, choose **Continue in your browser**. Leave the window open when it shows **Waiting for sign-in.**

Sign in with 8 West ID in the browser if asked. Check your name, the business and the computer name if shown. Only connect if you just chose **Continue in your browser** in your own Westy window on the computer in front of you. If someone sent you the link or the details are wrong, close the browser page.
Choose **Connect Westy** in the browser. When it says **Sign-in approved**, return to the Westy window and wait for your private chat to open.

blocks.text: **Expected result.** The Westy window shows your signed-in portal chat. It uses the computer tool permissions saved for your account.

**If you need help.** The sign-in link lasts only a short time. If it expired, start again from the Westy icon. If the page says your account cannot connect Westy, ask your administrator to check access for this business. If it says the computer is unavailable, ask your IT provider.

articles.title: Chat with Westy and choose your computer tool permissions
articles.summary: Ask for help in the Westy window and choose what Westy may do on a computer you can use.
ui_labels: New work when an earlier result is unknown

blocks.text: **Purpose and prerequisites.** Open Westy from its icon in the system tray on Windows or the menu bar on a Mac. Once connected, you can ask a question in its portal chat. A **Viewer** can ask for help. Work on a computer needs an account that can use its tools.

items: In the Westy window, open **Westy** if the chat is not already on screen. For help with a particular computer, check the name in the message box area. Use **Choose a computer** if you need to pick it.

If **Computer tool permissions** is shown, open it to review what Westy may use, such as **File access**, **Browser control** and **Desktop app control**. Turning off file access or ordinary repairs also turns off general commands. Your administrator’s limits still apply.

Under **New work when an earlier result is unknown**, pick **Allow — continue new authorized work** to allow other work, or **Deny — wait for unresolved work** to wait. Allow is the default. Neither choice repeats the earlier action. Choose **Save permissions** if you made a change.
Type your question or describe the work you want. Choose **Send message** and read the reply in the Westy window.

If **Computer control** appears after the reply and you want help in a window, select the **Connected computer**. Fill in **Allowed websites** if the task uses a website. Choose **Allow a computer task**, then pick the window on your computer when asked.

blocks.text: **Expected result.** The reply appears in your private chat. A successful change shows **Your computer tool permissions are saved.** During a window task, **Stop computer control** lets you end control. Handle passwords, verification codes and administrator prompts yourself.

**If you need help.** If there is no connected computer, you can keep chatting. Open Westy on the intended computer and connect it. If that computer or its tools are still missing, ask your administrator or support team to check your access.

articles.title: Sign out of Westy on a shared computer
articles.summary: Close your private chat, check whether the computer disconnected and end the separate browser sign-in.
ui_labels: Open the customer portal in your browser
This page didn’t sign you out

blocks.text: **Purpose and prerequisites.** Open Westy from its icon in the system tray on Windows or the menu bar on a Mac. Use these steps before someone else uses the computer. Your Westy window and your web browser each have their own sign-in.

items: In the Westy window, find **Account** in the portal menu and choose **Sign out**.

Look for **You’re signed out of Westy** and read the line below it. If Westy could not confirm that the computer disconnected, the connection can stay open for up to 30 minutes. Quit Westy from its icon to end it right away in that case.

On a shared computer, choose **Open the customer portal in your browser**. If the browser is still signed in, use **Sign out** under **Account** there too. Finish signing out at 8 West ID if prompted.
When you want to connect again, open Westy from its icon. From your own window choose **Continue in your browser** if asked, check the account and computer, and complete the sign-in.

blocks.text: **Expected result.** Signing out closes your private chat in the Westy window. When the disconnect is confirmed, the page also says the computer is no longer connected to your account.

**If you need help.** If you see **This page didn’t sign you out**, choose **Go to the customer portal**, then use **Sign out** from its menu. If you still cannot end the connection, contact your support team.

articles.title: Set up two-factor authentication
articles.summary: Connect an authenticator app to 8 West ID and save the recovery codes you can use if you lose your phone.

blocks.text: **Purpose and prerequisites.** Two-factor authentication adds a code to your password sign-in. Some accounts require it. Have an authenticator app on your phone and a safe place to keep your recovery codes.

items: If a banner asks you to set up two-factor, choose **Set it up**. You can also open **Settings**, choose **Two-factor authentication**, then **Set up two-factor**. If sign-in opens the setup page for you, start there.

Find the code for 8 West ID in your app. Enter it in **Six-digit code from your app** and choose **Turn on two-factor**.

articles.title: Sign in with a code or get new recovery codes
articles.summary: Use an authenticator or recovery code, replace your backup codes, and manage which browsers can skip the code step.

blocks.text: **Purpose and prerequisites.** When 8 West ID asks for a code after your password, use your authenticator app or an unused recovery code. Once signed in, you can replace your recovery codes and manage trusted browsers.

items: At **Enter your code**, type the current code from your app in **Six-digit code**. If you have lost your phone, enter one unused recovery code in that same box. Each recovery code works once.
If you used an app code on a device only you use, you can tick **Trust this browser** when offered. Choose **Continue**. Using a recovery code will not add this browser to your trusted list.

To get a fresh set, open **Settings** and choose **Two-factor authentication**. Enter **Code from your app** and choose **New recovery codes**. The new codes replace the old ones. Save the new set away from your phone before choosing **I have saved them**.
If **Trusted browsers** lists a browser you want to remove, choose **Remove** beside it. To ask for a code again on every trusted browser, choose **Remove all trusted browsers**.

blocks.text: **Expected result.** An accepted code lets you finish signing in. A trusted browser can skip the code step when you sign in with your password. Removing trust makes it ask for a code again.
**If you need help.** If a code fails, try the current one from your app. If you have lost both the app and your unused recovery codes, ask your account administrator for help with sign-in.

articles.title: Westy and your privacy
articles.summary: Your Westy conversation is private to your signed-in identity.
ui_labels: New work when an earlier result is unknown

body.text: Your Westy conversation is private to your signed-in identity. On an authorized connected computer, Westy can troubleshoot, run requested commands, work with files and control supported desktop/browser tools within your current account and device access. Computer tool permissions lets you choose Allow or Deny; Allow is the default and explicit Deny choices are honored. Windows elevation remains separate. Legacy Computer checks can also offer a specific repair with its own exact approval control. Visible operation receipts distinguish queued work from completed results. Stop reply stops generation; already dispatched device work keeps its own status. Only request text you review and send becomes a support record shared with you, client owners/admins and the support team.
